site.title: Remote Viewing
site.description: Practical guides on Remote Viewing, organized for fast browsing and comparison.

pages.title: Did Psychic Spying Ever Really Work?
pages.summary: Remote viewing is the claimed ability to describe a distant, hidden or future target without using the ordinary senses.

pages.title: 1995 Review
pages.summary: The 1995 review found disputed lab claims but no reliable intelligence value from operational remote viewing.

pages.summary: A significant result can flag an unusual pattern without proving that remote viewing caused it.

pages.title: Effect Sizes
pages.summary: Utts' case depended on repeated small shifts from chance, not dramatic hits in every session.

pages.title: Sketches
pages.summary: Remote viewing responses mix words, drawings, and impressions, which makes interpretation both useful and risky.

pages.title: Judging Rules
pages.summary: A remote-viewing sketch only gains evidential force when judging rules limit clues, editing bias, and selective scoring.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Sketches.

pages.title: Photo Targets
pages.summary: Photo-target trials show how free-response sketches were compared against real targets and plausible decoys.

pages.title: Raw Notes
pages.summary: Remote-viewing notes become more useful when sensory fragments are separated from confident labels that may be wrong.

pages.title: Rinconada
pages.summary: Pat Price's pool-complex account shows why vivid correct-looking details and absent imagined features must be judged together.

pages.title: Retrofit Risk
pages.summary: A circle, tower, or cluster of lines can look persuasive only after the target is known, making judging controls essential.

pages.title: Sketch Value
pages.summary: Sketches can keep layout and geometry visible before a viewer turns a vague form into a misleading noun.
